criteria.text: Symptoms suggest facet joint syndrome: no radiculopathy, pain worse with extension, rotation or lateral bending, and usually no neurologic deficit
Facet-mediated pain confirmed by provocative testing on exam (pain worse with extension and rotation)
Imaging suggests no other obvious cause of pain (e.g., fracture, tumor, infection, significant extraspinal lesion)
Pain limits daily activities
Pain has lasted more than 3 months (severe chronic back pain)
Pain has persisted despite at least 6 weeks of conservative treatment (systemic medications and/or physical therapy)
Radiofrequency facet neurolysis is being considered (diagnostic blocks are not medically necessary otherwise)
No untreated radiculopathy. Diagnostic blocks for back pain with untreated radiculopathy are E/I/U
No more than 3 facet levels per session (up to 6 injections if bilateral)
Second (confirmatory) block only at the same level(s) as the first, and only if the first gave >=80% relief of facet-mediated pain for at least the expected duration of the local anesthetic
No additional sets beyond the two diagnostic blocks at the same levels and side (E/I/U)
Therapeutic facet injections or MBBs (any steroid-containing facet injection counts as therapeutic) are E/I/U
Only one invasive back pain modality or procedure is medically necessary at a time
Fluoroscopic/CT guidance. Ultrasound-guided facet injections (0216T-0218T) are E/I/U

criteria.text: Radiculopathy: pain, dysesthesias or paresthesias in a named dermatomal distribution causing significant functional limits (reduced quality of life, impaired ADLs)

Radiculopathy corroborated by EITHER a detailed neuro exam within the prior 3 months (named-muscle/myotomal weakness, dermatomal sensory change, or diminished/absent/asymmetric reflexes) OR, within the prior 12 months, concordant MRI/CT showing compression of the named root or EMG/NCV diagnostic of root compression
Non-invasive measures (e.g., physical therapy, non-narcotic analgesics) have failed or are not tolerated
Radicular pain is consistent with radiologic findings (initial therapeutic TFESI)
Fluoroscopic or CT guidance. Ultrasound-guided TFESI is E/I/U
Therapeutic TFESI is given as part of a comprehensive pain management program

Repeat TFESI requires at least 2 of the following for >=2 weeks after the prior injection: >=50% pain relief; better function/activity (e.g., return to work); less pain medication and/or fewer other services (PT/chiropractic)
No more than 2 contiguous levels per session, and no more than 4 TFESIs per session (2 bilateral at 2 contiguous levels in one region)
No more than 3 TFESI sessions per episode of pain per region in 6 months (no more than 12 TFESIs in those 3 sessions)
No more than 4 TFESI sessions per region per 12 months
Sessions no more often than every 2 weeks
Not combined with pulsed RF, with RFA for disc herniation, or with a caudal ESI (all E/I/U)
Only one invasive back pain modality or procedure is medically necessary at a time

criteria.text: Careful screening, evaluation and diagnosis by a multidisciplinary team before implantation, including psychological and physical evaluations
No untreated substance use disorder (per ASAM guidelines)
Clearance from a psychiatrist, psychologist or other qualified mental health professional (e.g., LCSW)
More conservative pain management tried and failed for at least 6 months
Medications include at least 3 classes: NSAIDs, TCAs, SSRIs, SNRIs, muscle relaxants (tizanidine, cyclobenzaprine, baclofen), anticonvulsants

Formal in-person (not virtual) PT with a licensed physical therapist for at least 6 weeks within the past year. Waived if the PT discharge note documents that further PT is not useful because of exceptional pain
Psychological therapies tried as part of conservative care
If the patient has had spinal surgery: at least 6 months post-op
Functional disability on the Oswestry Disability Index: ODI >=21%
CT or MRI of the thoracic spine shows no anatomic contraindication to lead placement
Other reasonable pain sources ruled out, including significant pathology at other spinal levels on the advanced imaging report
Permanent implant requires >=50% pain reduction during a 3- to 7-day percutaneous trial, documented by the trial placement and lead-pull notes
Trial limited to 16 contacts, 2 percutaneous leads, or 1 paddle lead
A repeat trial after a failed trial is not medically necessary unless there were extenuating circumstances (e.g., lead migration, infection, anatomic difficulty)

MA criteria exceed NCD 160.7 / LCD L37632 (possible appeal basis under CMS-4201-F): CPB 0194 limits SCS to (1) FBSS with low back pain and significant radicular pain, (2) CRPS I/II, (3) inoperable ischemic limb pain, or (4) last-resort neuropathic pain from listed causes (arachnoiditis, phantom limb, peripheral neuropathy incl. diabetic, PHN, intercostal neuralgia, cauda equina injury, incomplete SCI, plexopathy). criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe low back pain primarily over the SIJ, between the upper iliac crests and the gluteal fold
Low back pain duration at least 3 months
Pain below L5 without radiculopathy

Clinical findings/imaging do not suggest another cause (central stenosis with claudication/myelopathy, foraminal stenosis or disc herniation with concordant radiculopathy, infection, tumor, fracture, pseudoarthrosis, hardware pain)
>=3 positive provocative maneuvers among FABER, Gaenslen, thigh thrust/posterior shear, SI compression, SI distraction, Yeoman
Pain persists despite at least 4 weeks of conservative therapy
Performed with conservative treatment; patient actively participating in rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
Coexisting psychological conditions/depression treated and stabilized before the procedure
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Not performed with other lumbosacral musculoskeletal injections or other blocks in the same session or during the post-SIJI assessment period
Index pain measured pre-injection at start of session and post-injection at end of session, same scale
Diagnostic SIJI positive only if >=75% sustained relief of index pain for the duration of the anesthetic (and of the steroid), on the same scale, with dated measurements on the following days
No more than 2 diagnostic SIJI sessions (unilateral or bilateral); no subsequent diagnostic SIJI if the first gave <75% relief
Therapeutic SIJI only after a diagnostic SIJI with >=75% relief
Repeat therapeutic SIJI requires >=50% pain relief or >=50% ADL improvement for >=3 months from the prior SIJI vs baseline (same scale)
No more than 4 therapeutic SIJI sessions per rolling 12 months (each side on a separate day counts as a session)
SIJI beyond 12 months requires significant functional disability, >=50% sustained improvement for >=3 months, documented rationale, and PCP notification
Fluoroscopic images in >=2 views (pre/post contrast, AP and oblique) confirming intra-articular contrast retained
Relief documentation states specific dates, same scale, and whether duration is consistent with the agent used (a bare % is insufficient)
KX on diagnostic injections; physician bills 27096 (bilateral = modifier 50); hospital OPD/ASC facility bills G0260

open_questions: Alliant publishes no medical policy for facet joint injections or medial branch blocks on alliantplans.com (no medical policy documents are listed in its public document library). Per the 2026 Provider Manual, reviews apply the Certificate of Coverage, Alliant Medical Policy, Alliant UM Guidelines and InterQual criteria. InterQual is proprietary and not public. The manual says providers may ask UM at (800) 865-5922 for a copy of specific criteria. No clinical criteria are included in this entry until that copy is obtained.

The March 2026 PA list names facet injections under 'Pain Management Invasive Procedures' but gives no CPT codes. Whether 64493, 64494 and 64495 each need PA, and whether the add-on codes (64494/64495) are reviewed separately from 64493, is not confirmed. The Prior Authorization Verification Tool asks for provider Group Name, Tax ID and User, so it was not used.

No vendor delegation (eviCore, Carelon, Evolent, TurningPoint, etc.) appears in any public Alliant document; the Provider Manual describes in-house Alliant nurse reviewers with Clinical Reviewer / Medical Director referral. Confirm by phone.

Retro policy conflict: the 2026 Provider Manual says retrospective requests are not considered and same-day requests are not accepted. The PA fax form (1/1/25) says a past date of service is handled as a post-service request with a documented reason. Confirm which applies.
Whether PA rules differ for 4Corners level-funded plans, SoloCare HMO, or PHCS-network members beyond the member-responsibility rule in the COCs is not confirmed.
No Alliant-sourced supporting ICD-10 list; supporting_icd10 left empty.

criteria.text: Pain causing functional disability or average pain >=6/10 related to the lumbar region
Pain duration >=3 months
Pain by history mainly axial/non-radicular (or radicular only from imaging-confirmed synovial cyst stenosis)
Primary source is not SI joint, discogenic, disc herniation, or radiculitis
If chronic lumbar spondylolysis is the diagnosis: imaging confirms pars defect
Failed >=6 weeks of conservative treatment in the last 6 months targeting the lumbar region (or documented medical reason it cannot be done)
Conservative treatment = >=1 active (PT, physician-supervised HEP, chiropractic) + >=1 inactive (medications, injections, TENS/bracing) component
HEP counts only with documented exercise prescription from MD/PT/DC and follow-up documenting completion after 6 weeks (or medical reason unable)
Failure = no meaningful improvement after full course, worsening during treatment, or documented medical inability (office closure/inconvenience/unexplained noncompliance do not count)
If prior spinal injections in the region: document ongoing engagement in conservative treatment instead
Performed under imaging guidance (fluoroscopy or CT; ultrasound only if CT/fluoro contraindicated)
Diagnostic phase: max 2 diagnostic injections, no sooner than 2 weeks apart
Second diagnostic block at same level requires >=50% relief or significant functional improvement from the first
Second diagnostic block may target a different level/technique only if first gave no relief and pain generator is uncertain or multilevel pathology
If most recent injection was local-anesthetic-only diagnostic block: >=7 days between injections
Max 4 facet injections per 12 months per spinal region
Right and left unilateral injections at same level within 1 month count as one procedure
RFA candidacy requires >=70% relief (or improved function) from a medial branch block; intra-articular facet injection does not qualify for RFA
Repeat diagnostic block after prior RFA only if pain generator in question, different levels, or surgery in the region
Different spinal regions: >=7 days apart unless medical reason documented; no different injection types same region same day (except facet + ESI for imaging-confirmed synovial cyst)
Injection >=2 years after prior injection in region (or after surgery/new pathology) = new episode; initial criteria apply
Submit recent office notes, prior imaging results, prior IPM procedure dates/results, conservative care details, and 0-10 pain scores/functional impact

criteria.text: Pain causing functional disability or average pain >=6/10 related to the lumbar region
Indication is one of: acute radicular pain/exacerbation of chronic radicular pain; spinal stenosis with axial or radicular pain; failed back surgery syndrome/epidural fibrosis
Acute/exacerbation pathway: radicular symptoms with pain duration <3 months
Acute/exacerbation pathway: failed >=2 weeks conservative treatment targeting lumbar region (active therapy not required) or documented reason
Stenosis or FBSS pathway: failed >=6 weeks conservative treatment in last 6 months (>=1 active + >=1 inactive) or documented reason
FBSS pathway: documented medical reason why injection is needed (not typically immediately post-op)
If prior spinal injections in region: document engagement in ongoing conservative treatment
Failure = no meaningful improvement, worsening, or documented medical inability (closure/inconvenience/unexplained noncompliance do not count)
Fluoroscopic guidance required for transforaminal injections
No more than 2 transforaminal levels in one day
Initial phase: up to 3 injections >=2 weeks apart, each repeat requires >=30% relief or significant functional improvement
If an initial-phase injection fails, next may be at a different level/technique when pain generator uncertain or multilevel pathology
Therapeutic phase: >=50% relief or significant functional improvement for >=2 months before each repeat
Therapeutic phase: continued pain >=6/10 or functional disability, and engaged in ongoing active conservative treatment
First year: max 6 epidural injections per region (3 initial + 3 therapeutic)
After first year: max 4 per 12 months per region (max 6 with documented special circumstances, e.g., elderly non-operative severe stenosis)
Different spinal regions >=7 days apart unless medical reason; no different injection types same region same day (except ESI + facet for synovial cyst)
Diagnostic TF injection for surgical planning requires documented pre-operative evaluation and surgical plan
Injection >=2 years after prior in region (or after surgery/new pathology) = new episode
Each epidural injection requires its own authorization
Submit office notes, imaging results, prior IPM dates/results, conservative care details and outcomes, 0-10 pain/function

criteria.text: Significant radicular pain in a specific dermatomal distribution, radiculopathy, or neurogenic claudication with associated functional impairment and completed physical exam
Significant pain = >=3/10 with inability to perform >=2 ADLs/IADLs
MRI or CT shows nerve root compression from herniated disc (imaging within 18 months) or spinal stenosis, correlating with clinical findings; required for transforaminal approach
Imaging performed and read by an independent radiologist
Radicular pain unresponsive to >=4 weeks conservative management (>=2 weeks if clear radiculopathy: dermatomal sensory change, myotomal weakness, and/or reflex abnormality)

Conservative management = PT (qualified provider, or supervised tailored HEP with MD/DO/PT instruction, redemonstration and documented compliance, or documented exception) AND >=1 complementary strategy (anti-inflammatories/analgesics, nerve membrane stabilizers/muscle relaxants, or acupuncture/chiropractic/massage/activity modification/rest)
Fluoroscopy or CT with contrast to confirm needle placement (unless contraindicated)
Max 2 transforaminal injections per session (one level bilateral or two levels unilateral)
One spinal region per date of service; no interlaminar/caudal with TF same session; no other spine procedure same day (except facet synovial cyst aspiration)
Max 4 therapeutic sessions per region per rolling 12 months regardless of approach/levels
Repeat = prior injection within 12 months; >=12 months = new initial injection
Repeat: prior injection gave >=50% pain reduction and functional improvement for >=3 months documented at follow-up
Repeat: imaging shows compression/stenosis at requested levels and laterality (HNP imaging within 18 months; no repeat imaging for fixed stenosis)
Repeat: patient continues conservative management between injections
If initial gives <50% relief within 2 weeks: one-time second injection >=2 weeks later with different approach, level, or steroid, rationale documented
Notify PCP if procedures continue beyond 12 months/prolonged repeat steroid use

Evaluate first if new pain with malignancy/infection/osteoporotic fracture risk, coagulopathy/anticoagulation, acute trauma; contraindicated in cauda equina/conus syndrome, epidural abscess/hematoma/mass, spinal fracture <6 weeks, systemic or local infection, uncontrolled diabetes
Preauthorization required for coverage of all pain management services and procedures before service; clinical documentation submitted with request

criteria.text: Persistent, typically unilateral non-radicular pain predominantly below L5, primarily localized over SI joint region, >=3 months
Localized tenderness over sacral sulcus just inferior to PSIS without tenderness of equal severity elsewhere (lumbar spine, greater trochanter, hip, coccyx)
>=1 positive provocative test (pelvic distraction, lateral iliac compression, sacral compression/thrust, thigh thrust, FABER/Patrick, Gaenslen)
No acute/subacute radicular pain, radiculopathy, or neurogenic claudication (or it is addressed, stable, and maximally optimized)

Significant pain = >=3/10 with inability to perform >=2 ADLs/IADLs

Diagnostic (anesthetic-only) injection only to confirm SIJ as pain generator before planned SIJ fusion

Therapeutic: corticosteroid +/- anesthetic, total volume <=2.5 cc; document biphasic response and 24-hour pain diary if steroid given
Repeat = prior injection within 12 months
Repeat: symptoms recur and prior injection gave >=50% relief and ADL improvement for >=3 months; repeat exam confirms SIJ source
Max 4 injections per 12 months
Therapeutic injections accompanied by ongoing active rehab/HEP/functional restoration program
Not on same day as other spine injection procedures
Notify PCP if continued beyond 12 months/prolonged steroid use

criteria.text: Significant radicular pain in a dermatomal distribution, radiculopathy, or neurogenic claudication with functional impairment and completed physical exam
Significant pain = >=3/10 with inability to perform >=2 ADLs/IADLs
MRI or CT shows nerve root compression from herniated disc (within 18 months) or spinal stenosis, correlating with clinical findings; required for transforaminal approach
Imaging performed and read by an independent radiologist

Conservative management = PT (qualified provider, or supervised tailored HEP with MD/DO/PT instruction and documented compliance, or documented exception) AND >=1 complementary strategy
Fluoroscopy or CT with contrast to confirm needle placement (unless contraindicated)
Max 2 transforaminal injections per session (one level bilateral or two levels unilateral)
One spinal region per date of service; no interlaminar/caudal with TF same session; no other spine procedure same day (except synovial cyst aspiration)
Max 4 therapeutic sessions per region per rolling 12 months regardless of approach/levels
Repeat = prior injection within 12 months; >=12 months = new initial injection
Repeat: prior injection gave >=50% pain reduction and functional improvement for >=3 months documented at follow-up
Repeat: imaging shows compression/stenosis at requested levels and laterality (HNP imaging within 18 months; no repeat imaging for fixed stenosis)
Repeat: patient continues conservative management between injections
If initial gives <50% relief within 2 weeks: one-time second injection >=2 weeks later with different approach, level, or steroid, rationale documented
Notify PCP if procedures continue beyond 12 months/prolonged repeat steroid use
Evaluate first if new pain with malignancy/infection/fracture risk, coagulopathy/anticoagulation, acute trauma; contraindicated in cauda equina, epidural abscess/hematoma, uncontrolled diabetes, etc.

Anthem says MA determinations follow CMS NCD/LCD hierarchy, but Carelon applies its own guideline 'when existing guidance does not provide sufficient clinical detail' - Carelon IPM criteria (e.g., >=50% relief x 3 months for repeat ESI, 4 sessions/region/12 months) may be applied where Palmetto LCDs are silent.

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe chronic neck pain, predominantly axial
Pain causes functional deficit measured on a pain or disability scale
Pain present for at least 3 months

Documented failure to respond to non-invasive conservative management as tolerated (NSAIDs, acetaminophen, PT, acupuncture [chronic LBP only], or spinal manipulation, incl. biopsychosocial techniques)
No untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication (except radiculopathy caused by a facet synovial cyst)
No non-facet pathology on clinical assessment or imaging that could explain the pain (e.g., fracture, tumor, infection, significant deformity)
Baseline pain scale AND baseline disability scale documented; same pain scale repeated after each diagnostic procedure
Not for generalized or centralized pain conditions (e.g., fibromyalgia)
Diagnostic MBB performed with intent to proceed to RFA at the diagnosed level(s) if positive
MBB is the diagnostic block of choice; IA diagnostic block only if MBB cannot be done due to documented anatomic restriction
Second (confirmatory) diagnostic MBB at the same level only after the first gave a consistent >=80% relief of primary (index) pain, duration consistent with the agent used
Confirmatory MBB at least 2 weeks after the first diagnostic block (exceptions individually documented)
No more than 4 diagnostic facet sessions per spinal region per rolling 12 months
If >=2 years since last RFA and the source of recurrent pain is in question, diagnostic blocks must be repeated
Therapeutic (non-diagnostic) MBB only after 2 diagnostic blocks each >=80% relief AND documentation of why the patient is not an RFA candidate (e.g., pseudarthrosis, implanted electrical device)
Repeat therapeutic MBB requires >=50% relief for >=3 months (or >=50% improvement in ADLs vs baseline, same scale); max 4 therapeutic sessions per region per rolling 12 months
No moderate/deep sedation, general anesthesia, or MAC for MBB
Append KX modifier to diagnostic facet injection lines; bilateral = 1 unit with modifier 50
1-2 levels (unilateral or bilateral) per session per spinal region; 3-4 level procedures non-covered
Facet interventions limited to 1 spinal region per session (cervical/thoracic or lumbar/sacral)
Performed under fluoroscopic or CT guidance (no guidance, ultrasound, or MRI guidance not covered)
Other blocks (ESI, TPI, sympathetic) on the same day not expected; if done, medical necessity of each documented

criteria.text: History, physical exam, AND concordant imaging (CT/MRI) support lumbar radiculopathy, radicular pain and/or neurogenic claudication from disc herniation, osteophyte complex, or severe DDD causing foraminal/central stenosis; OR post-laminectomy syndrome; OR acute herpes zoster pain
Radicular pain/neurogenic claudication severe enough to greatly impact quality of life or function
Objective pain scale or functional assessment at baseline; same scale repeated at each follow-up
Pain duration at least 4 weeks
Failure of 4 weeks of noninvasive conservative care, or documented inability to tolerate it (4-week wait waived for refractory acute herpes zoster)
ESI given in conjunction with conservative treatment; patient in active rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound without contrast only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Repeat ESI requires >=50% pain relief for >=3 months, or >=50% improvement in ability to perform previously painful movements/ADLs vs baseline on the same scale
If the initial ESI fails, one repeat after 14 days with a different approach, level, and/or medication, with rationale documented
Max 4 ESI sessions per spinal region per rolling 12 months, regardless of levels
ESI beyond 12 months requires significant functional/vocational disability, >=50% sustained improvement, documented rationale for continuing, and PCP notification
No predetermined series of ESIs
Only 1 spinal region per session
ILESI max 1 level per session; bilateral ILESI not reasonable and necessary (62323 is not a bilateral procedure)
No other blocks (facet, sympathetic, TPI) in the same session (except facet synovial cyst + ESI)
Moderate/deep sedation, GA, or MAC not routinely covered; exceptional need must be clearly documented
No contraindication: suspected/active local spinal infection, significant systemic infection, compressive lesion of cord/conus/cauda equina, suspicion or major risk factors for cancer
Retain films (>=2 views) documenting final needle position and contrast flow

criteria.text: History, physical exam, AND concordant imaging (CT/MRI) support lumbar radiculopathy, radicular pain and/or neurogenic claudication from disc herniation, osteophyte complex, or severe DDD causing foraminal/central stenosis; OR post-laminectomy syndrome; OR acute herpes zoster pain

Objective pain scale or functional assessment at baseline; same scale repeated at each follow-up

Only 1 spinal region per session

No other blocks (facet, sympathetic, TPI) in the same session (except facet synovial cyst + ESI)
Moderate/deep sedation, GA, or MAC not routinely covered; exceptional need must be clearly documented

criteria.text: Chronic intractable pain
SCS used only as a late resort (if not a last resort)
Other modalities (pharmacological, surgical, physical, psychological) tried and unsatisfactory, or judged unsuitable/contraindicated
Careful screening, evaluation, and diagnosis by a multidisciplinary team before implantation, including psychological AND physical evaluation
All facilities, equipment, and professional/support personnel for diagnosis, treatment training, and follow-up available
Record documents the elements leading to the diagnosis and the therapies tried before deciding on SCS
Billing article A56876 has no ICD-10 diagnosis restriction; coverage rests on NCD 160.7 conditions
Max 2 leads or 16 contacts reimbursed
Max 2 SCS trials per anatomic spinal region per lifetime (63650: 2 per DOS, 4 units lifetime), except technical limitation or different stimulation modality/new technology
Repeat trial after a failed trial only with documented extenuating circumstances (on appeal)
Office trial only if sterility/equipment/staff available AND physician has like privileges at a local hospital/ASC or is ABA-subspecialty boarded in Pain Medicine
If the trialing physician will not implant the permanent system, the patient is informed in writing with the name of the implanting surgeon

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe low back pain primarily over the SIJ, between the upper iliac crests and the gluteal fold
Low back pain duration at least 3 months
Pain below L5 without radiculopathy

Clinical findings/imaging do not suggest another cause (central stenosis with claudication/myelopathy, foraminal stenosis or disc herniation with concordant radiculopathy, infection, tumor, fracture, pseudoarthrosis, hardware pain)
>=3 positive provocative maneuvers among FABER, Gaenslen, thigh thrust/posterior shear, SI compression, SI distraction, Yeoman
Pain persists despite at least 4 weeks of conservative therapy
Performed with conservative treatment; patient actively participating in rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
Coexisting psychological conditions/depression treated and stabilized before the procedure
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Not performed with other lumbosacral musculoskeletal injections or other blocks in the same session or during the post-SIJI assessment period
Index pain measured pre-injection at start of session and post-injection at end of session, same scale
Diagnostic SIJI positive only if >=75% sustained relief of index pain for the duration of the anesthetic (and of the steroid), on the same scale, with dated measurements on the following days
No more than 2 diagnostic SIJI sessions (unilateral or bilateral); no subsequent diagnostic SIJI if the first gave <75% relief
Therapeutic SIJI only after a diagnostic SIJI with >=75% relief
Repeat therapeutic SIJI requires >=50% pain relief or >=50% ADL improvement for >=3 months from the prior SIJI vs baseline (same scale)
No more than 4 therapeutic SIJI sessions per rolling 12 months (each side on a separate day counts as a session)
SIJI beyond 12 months requires significant functional disability, >=50% sustained improvement for >=3 months, documented rationale, and PCP notification
Fluoroscopic images in >=2 views (pre/post contrast, AP and oblique) confirming intra-articular contrast retained
Relief documentation states specific dates, same scale, and whether duration is consistent with the agent used (a bare % is insufficient)
KX on diagnostic injections; physician bills 27096 (bilateral = modifier 50); hospital OPD/ASC facility bills G0260

criteria.text: Radiofrequency ablation is being considered as the therapeutic intervention (diagnostic MBB not medically necessary otherwise)

Routine therapeutic MBBs for chronic pain are not authorized; intra-articular facet injections are not medically necessary and do not qualify as diagnostic for neurotomy

criteria.text: Initial RFA: all MBB clinical criteria (MM-0974 I.A.1-10) met within the past 36 months

criteria.text: History, physical exam, AND concordant imaging (CT/MRI) support lumbar radiculopathy, radicular pain and/or neurogenic claudication from disc herniation, osteophyte complex, or severe DDD causing foraminal/central stenosis; OR post-laminectomy syndrome; OR acute herpes zoster pain

Objective pain scale or functional assessment at baseline; same scale repeated at each follow-up
Pain duration at least 4 weeks

Only 1 spinal region per session

No other blocks (facet, sympathetic, TPI) in the same session (except facet synovial cyst + ESI)
Moderate/deep sedation, GA, or MAC not routinely covered; exceptional need must be clearly documented

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain, predominantly axial

No moderate/deep sedation, general anesthesia, or MAC for MBB
Append KX modifier to diagnostic facet injection lines; bilateral = 1 unit with modifier 50
1-2 levels (unilateral or bilateral) per session per spinal region; 3-4 level procedures non-covered
Facet interventions limited to 1 spinal region per session (cervical/thoracic or lumbar/sacral)
Performed under fluoroscopic or CT guidance (no guidance, ultrasound, or MRI guidance not covered)
Other blocks (ESI, TPI, sympathetic) on the same day not expected; if done, medical necessity of each documented

criteria.text: History, physical exam, AND concordant imaging (CT/MRI) support lumbar radiculopathy, radicular pain and/or neurogenic claudication from disc herniation, osteophyte complex, or severe DDD causing foraminal/central stenosis; OR post-laminectomy syndrome; OR acute herpes zoster pain
Radicular pain/neurogenic claudication severe enough to greatly impact quality of life or function
Objective pain scale or functional assessment at baseline; same scale repeated at each follow-up
Pain duration at least 4 weeks
Failure of 4 weeks of noninvasive conservative care, or documented inability to tolerate it (4-week wait waived for refractory acute herpes zoster)
ESI given in conjunction with conservative treatment; patient in active rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound without contrast only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Repeat ESI requires >=50% pain relief for >=3 months, or >=50% improvement in ability to perform previously painful movements/ADLs vs baseline on the same scale
If the initial ESI fails, one repeat after 14 days with a different approach, level, and/or medication, with rationale documented
Max 4 ESI sessions per spinal region per rolling 12 months, regardless of levels
ESI beyond 12 months requires significant functional/vocational disability, >=50% sustained improvement, documented rationale for continuing, and PCP notification
No predetermined series of ESIs
Only 1 spinal region per session
TFESI max 2 levels in 1 region per session (unilateral or bilateral); bilateral only when clinically indicated; bilateral = 1 line with modifier 50
No other blocks (facet, sympathetic, TPI) in the same session (except facet synovial cyst + ESI)
Moderate/deep sedation, GA, or MAC not routinely covered; exceptional need must be clearly documented
No contraindication: suspected/active local spinal infection, significant systemic infection, compressive lesion of cord/conus/cauda equina, suspicion or major risk factors for cancer
TFESI procedure report documents indication, medical necessity, and baseline pain score; retain films (>=2 views) of final needle position and contrast flow

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe low back pain primarily over the SIJ, between the upper iliac crests and the gluteal fold
Low back pain duration at least 3 months
Pain below L5 without radiculopathy

Clinical findings/imaging do not suggest another cause (central stenosis with claudication/myelopathy, foraminal stenosis or disc herniation with concordant radiculopathy, infection, tumor, fracture, pseudoarthrosis, hardware pain)
>=3 positive provocative maneuvers among FABER, Gaenslen, thigh thrust/posterior shear, SI compression, SI distraction, Yeoman
Pain persists despite at least 4 weeks of conservative therapy
Performed with conservative treatment; patient actively participating in rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
Coexisting psychological conditions/depression treated and stabilized before the procedure
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Not performed with other lumbosacral musculoskeletal injections or other blocks in the same session or during the post-SIJI assessment period
Index pain measured pre-injection at start of session and post-injection at end of session, same scale
Diagnostic SIJI positive only if >=75% sustained relief of index pain for the duration of the anesthetic (and of the steroid), on the same scale, with dated measurements on the following days
No more than 2 diagnostic SIJI sessions (unilateral or bilateral); no subsequent diagnostic SIJI if the first gave <75% relief
Therapeutic SIJI only after a diagnostic SIJI with >=75% relief
Repeat therapeutic SIJI requires >=50% pain relief or >=50% ADL improvement for >=3 months from the prior SIJI vs baseline (same scale)
No more than 4 therapeutic SIJI sessions per rolling 12 months (each side on a separate day counts as a session)
SIJI beyond 12 months requires significant functional disability, >=50% sustained improvement for >=3 months, documented rationale, and PCP notification
Fluoroscopic images in >=2 views (pre/post contrast, AP and oblique) confirming intra-articular contrast retained
Relief documentation states specific dates, same scale, and whether duration is consistent with the agent used (a bare % is insufficient)
KX on diagnostic injections; physician bills 27096 (bilateral = modifier 50); hospital OPD/ASC facility bills G0260

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain, predominantly axial
Pain causes functional deficit measured on a pain or disability scale
Pain present for at least 3 months

Documented failure to respond to non-invasive conservative management as tolerated (NSAIDs, acetaminophen, PT, acupuncture [chronic LBP only], or spinal manipulation, incl. biopsychosocial techniques)
No untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication (except radiculopathy caused by a facet synovial cyst)
No non-facet pathology on clinical assessment or imaging that could explain the pain (e.g., fracture, tumor, infection, significant deformity)
Baseline pain scale AND baseline disability scale documented; same pain scale repeated after each diagnostic procedure
Not for generalized or centralized pain conditions (e.g., fibromyalgia)
Initial RFA only after at least 2 medically necessary diagnostic MBBs, each with consistent >=80% sustained relief of primary (index) pain, duration consistent with the agent used
Repeat RFA at the same site requires >=50% improvement in pain for >=6 months, or >=50% improvement in ability to perform previously painful movements/ADLs vs baseline on the same scale
No more than 2 RFA sessions per spinal region per rolling 12 months
If >=2 years since last RFA and the source of recurrent pain is in question, repeat diagnostic MBBs before RFA
Thermal radiofrequency (>=80 degrees C) only; pulsed RF, chemical, low-grade thermal, laser, and cryoablation are non-covered (bill 64999)
Moderate sedation only with documented medical necessity (e.g., inability to cooperate/remain motionless); anxiety or preference alone insufficient; no routine MAC/GA/deep sedation
RFA codes reported per joint, not per nerve; bilateral = 1 unit with modifier 50
1-2 levels (unilateral or bilateral) per session per spinal region; 3-4 level procedures non-covered
Facet interventions limited to 1 spinal region per session (cervical/thoracic or lumbar/sacral)
Performed under fluoroscopic or CT guidance (no guidance, ultrasound, or MRI guidance not covered)
Other blocks (ESI, TPI, sympathetic) on the same day not expected; if done, medical necessity of each documented

criteria.text: History, physical exam, AND concordant imaging (CT/MRI) support lumbar radiculopathy, radicular pain and/or neurogenic claudication from disc herniation, osteophyte complex, or severe DDD causing foraminal/central stenosis; OR post-laminectomy syndrome; OR acute herpes zoster pain
Radicular pain/neurogenic claudication severe enough to greatly impact quality of life or function
Objective pain scale or functional assessment at baseline; same scale repeated at each follow-up
Pain duration at least 4 weeks
Failure of 4 weeks of noninvasive conservative care, or documented inability to tolerate it (4-week wait waived for refractory acute herpes zoster)
ESI given in conjunction with conservative treatment; patient in active rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound without contrast only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Repeat ESI requires >=50% pain relief for >=3 months, or >=50% improvement in ability to perform previously painful movements/ADLs vs baseline on the same scale
If the initial ESI fails, one repeat after 14 days with a different approach, level, and/or medication, with rationale documented
Max 4 ESI sessions per spinal region per rolling 12 months, regardless of levels
ESI beyond 12 months requires significant functional/vocational disability, >=50% sustained improvement, documented rationale for continuing, and PCP notification
No predetermined series of ESIs
Only 1 spinal region per session
TFESI max 2 levels in 1 region per session (unilateral or bilateral); bilateral only when clinically indicated; bilateral = 1 line with modifier 50
No other blocks (facet, sympathetic, TPI) in the same session (except facet synovial cyst + ESI)
Moderate/deep sedation, GA, or MAC not routinely covered; exceptional need must be clearly documented
No contraindication: suspected/active local spinal infection, significant systemic infection, compressive lesion of cord/conus/cauda equina, suspicion or major risk factors for cancer
TFESI procedure report documents indication, medical necessity, and baseline pain score; retain films (>=2 views) of final needle position and contrast flow

Exceeds NCD 160.7 but matches A56876, so NOT an appeal basis in GA: Humana's lifetime limit of 2 SCS leads and 2 trials per anatomic spinal region (exceptions for technical limitation or a different modality/new technology). A56876 has the same trial limit and a maximum of 2 leads or 16 contacts.

humana_ma_hum1215_008 applies its indication list, 6-month pain duration, pain-focused psychological evaluation, >=3-day trial and >=50% pain-reduction criteria only in jurisdictions WITHOUT an LCD. In GA (JJ), L37632 governs those points, so they are not labeled.

Cohere items stricter than L37632 (not labeled because they are not shown to apply to Humana): psych evaluation within 12 months; >3 months failed conservative care within 12 months incl. 2 neuropathic meds and an interventional procedure; spine/vascular surgeon non-candidacy evaluation within 12 months for FBSS, back/neck pain and limb ischemia; PDN: HbA1c <=9 within 3 months and glucose control optimized; trial >=3 days; active substance use disorder excluded; DRG only for lower-extremity CRPS. criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe low back pain primarily over the SIJ, between the upper iliac crests and the gluteal fold
Low back pain duration at least 3 months
Pain below L5 without radiculopathy

Clinical findings/imaging do not suggest another cause (central stenosis with claudication/myelopathy, foraminal stenosis or disc herniation with concordant radiculopathy, infection, tumor, fracture, pseudoarthrosis, hardware pain)
>=3 positive provocative maneuvers among FABER, Gaenslen, thigh thrust/posterior shear, SI compression, SI distraction, Yeoman
Pain persists despite at least 4 weeks of conservative therapy
Performed with conservative treatment; patient actively participating in rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
Coexisting psychological conditions/depression treated and stabilized before the procedure
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Not performed with other lumbosacral musculoskeletal injections or other blocks in the same session or during the post-SIJI assessment period
Index pain measured pre-injection at start of session and post-injection at end of session, same scale
Diagnostic SIJI positive only if >=75% sustained relief of index pain for the duration of the anesthetic (and of the steroid), on the same scale, with dated measurements on the following days
No more than 2 diagnostic SIJI sessions (unilateral or bilateral); no subsequent diagnostic SIJI if the first gave <75% relief
Therapeutic SIJI only after a diagnostic SIJI with >=75% relief
Repeat therapeutic SIJI requires >=50% pain relief or >=50% ADL improvement for >=3 months from the prior SIJI vs baseline (same scale)
No more than 4 therapeutic SIJI sessions per rolling 12 months (each side on a separate day counts as a session)
SIJI beyond 12 months requires significant functional disability, >=50% sustained improvement for >=3 months, documented rationale, and PCP notification
Fluoroscopic images in >=2 views (pre/post contrast, AP and oblique) confirming intra-articular contrast retained
Relief documentation states specific dates, same scale, and whether duration is consistent with the agent used (a bare % is insufficient)
KX on diagnostic injections; physician bills 27096 (bilateral = modifier 50); hospital OPD/ASC facility bills G0260

prior_auth.turnaround_note: Medicare FFS OPD prior authorization applies only when the procedure is done in a hospital outpatient department (type of bill 13X facility claim); not required in ASC, physician office, or critical access hospital. Facet codes on the CMS list: 64490, 64491, 64493, 64494, 64633, 64634, 64635, 64636 (64492/64495 removed 8/16/2024 as non-covered). The hospital OPD must obtain provisional affirmation (physician may submit on its behalf); only the OPD puts the UTN on its claim, but associated physician/anesthesia claims are denied if the OPD claim is denied for missing/non-affirmed PA. Each facet procedure needs its own request (UTN valid for one claim, 120 days). Decision within 7 calendar days (since 1/1/2025); expedited up to 2 business days. Affirmation does not override LCD frequency limits.

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe chronic neck pain, predominantly axial
Pain causes functional deficit measured on a pain or disability scale
Pain present for at least 3 months

Documented failure to respond to non-invasive conservative management as tolerated (NSAIDs, acetaminophen, PT, acupuncture [chronic LBP only], or spinal manipulation, incl. biopsychosocial techniques)
No untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication (except radiculopathy caused by a facet synovial cyst)
No non-facet pathology on clinical assessment or imaging that could explain the pain (e.g., fracture, tumor, infection, significant deformity)
Baseline pain scale AND baseline disability scale documented; same pain scale repeated after each diagnostic procedure
Not for generalized or centralized pain conditions (e.g., fibromyalgia)
Diagnostic MBB performed with intent to proceed to RFA at the diagnosed level(s) if positive
MBB is the diagnostic block of choice; IA diagnostic block only if MBB cannot be done due to documented anatomic restriction
Second (confirmatory) diagnostic MBB at the same level only after the first gave a consistent >=80% relief of primary (index) pain, duration consistent with the agent used
Confirmatory MBB at least 2 weeks after the first diagnostic block (exceptions individually documented)
No more than 4 diagnostic facet sessions per spinal region per rolling 12 months
If >=2 years since last RFA and the source of recurrent pain is in question, diagnostic blocks must be repeated
Therapeutic (non-diagnostic) MBB only after 2 diagnostic blocks each >=80% relief AND documentation of why the patient is not an RFA candidate (e.g., pseudarthrosis, implanted electrical device)
Repeat therapeutic MBB requires >=50% relief for >=3 months (or >=50% improvement in ADLs vs baseline, same scale); max 4 therapeutic sessions per region per rolling 12 months
No moderate/deep sedation, general anesthesia, or MAC for MBB
Append KX modifier to diagnostic facet injection lines; bilateral = 1 unit with modifier 50
1-2 levels (unilateral or bilateral) per session per spinal region; 3-4 level procedures non-covered
Facet interventions limited to 1 spinal region per session (cervical/thoracic or lumbar/sacral)
Performed under fluoroscopic or CT guidance (no guidance, ultrasound, or MRI guidance not covered)
Other blocks (ESI, TPI, sympathetic) on the same day not expected; if done, medical necessity of each documented

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe low back pain primarily over the SIJ, between the upper iliac crests and the gluteal fold
Low back pain duration at least 3 months
Pain below L5 without radiculopathy

Clinical findings/imaging do not suggest another cause (central stenosis with claudication/myelopathy, foraminal stenosis or disc herniation with concordant radiculopathy, infection, tumor, fracture, pseudoarthrosis, hardware pain)
>=3 positive provocative maneuvers among FABER, Gaenslen, thigh thrust/posterior shear, SI compression, SI distraction, Yeoman
Pain persists despite at least 4 weeks of conservative therapy
Performed with conservative treatment; patient actively participating in rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
Coexisting psychological conditions/depression treated and stabilized before the procedure
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Not performed with other lumbosacral musculoskeletal injections or other blocks in the same session or during the post-SIJI assessment period
Index pain measured pre-injection at start of session and post-injection at end of session, same scale
Diagnostic SIJI positive only if >=75% sustained relief of index pain for the duration of the anesthetic (and of the steroid), on the same scale, with dated measurements on the following days
No more than 2 diagnostic SIJI sessions (unilateral or bilateral); no subsequent diagnostic SIJI if the first gave <75% relief
Therapeutic SIJI only after a diagnostic SIJI with >=75% relief
Repeat therapeutic SIJI requires >=50% pain relief or >=50% ADL improvement for >=3 months from the prior SIJI vs baseline (same scale)
No more than 4 therapeutic SIJI sessions per rolling 12 months (each side on a separate day counts as a session)
SIJI beyond 12 months requires significant functional disability, >=50% sustained improvement for >=3 months, documented rationale, and PCP notification
Fluoroscopic images in >=2 views (pre/post contrast, AP and oblique) confirming intra-articular contrast retained
Relief documentation states specific dates, same scale, and whether duration is consistent with the agent used (a bare % is insufficient)
KX on diagnostic injections; physician bills 27096 (bilateral = modifier 50); hospital OPD/ASC facility bills G0260

criteria.text: Injection is for radicular back pain, shown by history and physical exam
Radicular pain has not responded to at least 4 weeks of conservative care: pharmacotherapy (e.g., NSAIDs or acetaminophen), OR activity modification, OR physical therapy/home exercise
Structural and/or functional nerve root involvement shown on imaging or electrodiagnostic studies
Done under fluoroscopic or CT guidance. Ultrasound guidance is not covered
No contraindication such as spinal neoplasm, rapidly progressing neurologic deficit, or epidural abscess
No more than 4 ESI sessions per region (lumbosacral) per year, regardless of level, location or side. A session is one date of service. The year is the 12 months from the first approved injection
Repeat ESI only if radicular pain has returned and/or function has worsened

Repeat ESI also requires ONE of: (a) prior injection gave >=50% pain relief or functional improvement for >=3 months on validated tools; or (b) prior injection gave <=50% relief for <3 months AND the patient, injection site and technique have been reassessed

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe chronic neck pain, predominantly axial
Pain causes functional deficit measured on a pain or disability scale
Pain present for at least 3 months

Documented failure to respond to non-invasive conservative management as tolerated (NSAIDs, acetaminophen, PT, acupuncture [chronic LBP only], or spinal manipulation, incl. biopsychosocial techniques)
No untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication (except radiculopathy caused by a facet synovial cyst)
No non-facet pathology on clinical assessment or imaging that could explain the pain (e.g., fracture, tumor, infection, significant deformity)
Baseline pain scale AND baseline disability scale documented; same pain scale repeated after each diagnostic procedure
Not for generalized or centralized pain conditions (e.g., fibromyalgia)
Diagnostic MBB performed with intent to proceed to RFA at the diagnosed level(s) if positive
MBB is the diagnostic block of choice; IA diagnostic block only if MBB cannot be done due to documented anatomic restriction
Second (confirmatory) diagnostic MBB at the same level only after the first gave a consistent >=80% relief of primary (index) pain, duration consistent with the agent used
Confirmatory MBB at least 2 weeks after the first diagnostic block (exceptions individually documented)
No more than 4 diagnostic facet sessions per spinal region per rolling 12 months
If >=2 years since last RFA and the source of recurrent pain is in question, diagnostic blocks must be repeated
Therapeutic (non-diagnostic) MBB only after 2 diagnostic blocks each >=80% relief AND documentation of why the patient is not an RFA candidate (e.g., pseudarthrosis, implanted electrical device)
Repeat therapeutic MBB requires >=50% relief for >=3 months (or >=50% improvement in ADLs vs baseline, same scale); max 4 therapeutic sessions per region per rolling 12 months
No moderate/deep sedation, general anesthesia, or MAC for MBB
Append KX modifier to diagnostic facet injection lines; bilateral = 1 unit with modifier 50
1-2 levels (unilateral or bilateral) per session per spinal region; 3-4 level procedures non-covered
Facet interventions limited to 1 spinal region per session (cervical/thoracic or lumbar/sacral)
Performed under fluoroscopic or CT guidance (no guidance, ultrasound, or MRI guidance not covered)
Other blocks (ESI, TPI, sympathetic) on the same day not expected; if done, medical necessity of each documented

criteria.text: History, physical exam, AND concordant imaging (CT/MRI) support lumbar radiculopathy, radicular pain and/or neurogenic claudication from disc herniation, osteophyte complex, or severe DDD causing foraminal/central stenosis; OR post-laminectomy syndrome; OR acute herpes zoster pain
Radicular pain/neurogenic claudication severe enough to greatly impact quality of life or function
Objective pain scale or functional assessment at baseline; same scale repeated at each follow-up
Pain duration at least 4 weeks
Failure of 4 weeks of noninvasive conservative care, or documented inability to tolerate it (4-week wait waived for refractory acute herpes zoster)
ESI given in conjunction with conservative treatment; patient in active rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound without contrast only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Repeat ESI requires >=50% pain relief for >=3 months, or >=50% improvement in ability to perform previously painful movements/ADLs vs baseline on the same scale
If the initial ESI fails, one repeat after 14 days with a different approach, level, and/or medication, with rationale documented
Max 4 ESI sessions per spinal region per rolling 12 months, regardless of levels
ESI beyond 12 months requires significant functional/vocational disability, >=50% sustained improvement, documented rationale for continuing, and PCP notification
No predetermined series of ESIs
Only 1 spinal region per session
ILESI max 1 level per session; bilateral ILESI not reasonable and necessary (62323 is not a bilateral procedure)
No other blocks (facet, sympathetic, TPI) in the same session (except facet synovial cyst + ESI)
Moderate/deep sedation, GA, or MAC not routinely covered; exceptional need must be clearly documented
No contraindication: suspected/active local spinal infection, significant systemic infection, compressive lesion of cord/conus/cauda equina, suspicion or major risk factors for cancer
Retain films (>=2 views) documenting final needle position and contrast flow

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain, predominantly axial
Pain causes functional deficit measured on a pain or disability scale
Pain present for at least 3 months

Documented failure to respond to non-invasive conservative management as tolerated (NSAIDs, acetaminophen, PT, acupuncture [chronic LBP only], or spinal manipulation, incl. biopsychosocial techniques)
No untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication (except radiculopathy caused by a facet synovial cyst)
No non-facet pathology on clinical assessment or imaging that could explain the pain (e.g., fracture, tumor, infection, significant deformity)
Baseline pain scale AND baseline disability scale documented; same pain scale repeated after each diagnostic procedure
Not for generalized or centralized pain conditions (e.g., fibromyalgia)
Diagnostic MBB performed with intent to proceed to RFA at the diagnosed level(s) if positive
MBB is the diagnostic block of choice; IA diagnostic block only if MBB cannot be done due to documented anatomic restriction
Second (confirmatory) diagnostic MBB at the same level only after the first gave a consistent >=80% relief of primary (index) pain, duration consistent with the agent used
Confirmatory MBB at least 2 weeks after the first diagnostic block (exceptions individually documented)
No more than 4 diagnostic facet sessions per spinal region per rolling 12 months
If >=2 years since last RFA and the source of recurrent pain is in question, diagnostic blocks must be repeated
Therapeutic (non-diagnostic) MBB only after 2 diagnostic blocks each >=80% relief AND documentation of why the patient is not an RFA candidate (e.g., pseudarthrosis, implanted electrical device)
Repeat therapeutic MBB requires >=50% relief for >=3 months (or >=50% improvement in ADLs vs baseline, same scale); max 4 therapeutic sessions per region per rolling 12 months
No moderate/deep sedation, general anesthesia, or MAC for MBB
Append KX modifier to diagnostic facet injection lines; bilateral = 1 unit with modifier 50
1-2 levels (unilateral or bilateral) per session per spinal region; 3-4 level procedures non-covered
Facet interventions limited to 1 spinal region per session (cervical/thoracic or lumbar/sacral)
Performed under fluoroscopic or CT guidance (no guidance, ultrasound, or MRI guidance not covered)
Other blocks (ESI, TPI, sympathetic) on the same day not expected; if done, medical necessity of each documented

MA criteria exceed NCD 160.7 (possible appeal basis under CMS-4201-F): MMP368.14 states a repeat trial after a failed trial is not appropriate unless extenuating circumstances led to the failure. Neither NCD 160.7 nor Palmetto LCD L37632 (v26) limits repeat trials. [uhc_ma_mmp368_14 vs NCD160.7, L37632]
Exceeds NCD 160.7 but matches Palmetto LCD L37632, so NOT an appeal basis in GA: trial must achieve ≥50% reduction of target pain or of analgesic medications.
Exceeds NCD 160.7 but matches L37632, so NOT an appeal basis in GA: trial must show some element of functional improvement.
Exceeds NCD 160.7 but matches L37632, so NOT an appeal basis in GA: chart documentation must support each trial-to-permanent-implant decision.
Same in NCD 160.7, L37632 and MMP368.14: multidisciplinary screening incl. psychological and physical evaluation; SCS as a late option after other modalities.
MMP368.14 applies its supplemental criteria only where no LCD/LCA exists. GA has Palmetto L37632 (+ billing article A56876), so L37632 is the controlling LCD for UHC MA in GA.
MMP368.14 and L37632 both say it is 'preferable' that the trialing physician implants the permanent device. Stated as a preference, not a coverage condition.

criteria.text: Chronic intractable pain
SCS used only as a late resort (if not a last resort)
Other modalities (pharmacological, surgical, physical, psychological) tried and unsatisfactory, or judged unsuitable/contraindicated
Careful screening, evaluation, and diagnosis by a multidisciplinary team before implantation, including psychological AND physical evaluation
All facilities, equipment, and professional/support personnel for diagnosis, treatment training, and follow-up available
Record documents the elements leading to the diagnosis and the therapies tried before deciding on SCS
Billing article A56876 has no ICD-10 diagnosis restriction; coverage rests on NCD 160.7 conditions
Max 2 leads or 16 contacts reimbursed
Pain relief demonstrated with a temporarily implanted electrode before permanent implantation
Successful trial: >=50% reduction of target pain OR >=50% reduction of analgesic medication, AND some element of functional improvement
Chart documentation supporting the decision to proceed from trial to permanent implant
Permanent neurostimulator placed in an ASC, outpatient hospital, or hospital (not office)
63655 (laminectomy/paddle) limited to 1 permanent SCS per patient per lifetime
Electronic analysis/programming (95970-95972) not more often than once every 30 days, except more frequent in the first month after implant

UHC list: 'Stimulators - Neurostimulator' 63650, 63655, 63685 require PA (Erickson Advantage excluded; use number on ID card). Members in delegated medical groups/IPAs follow the delegate's protocols.

not_covered_notes: 63661/63663 not reimbursed in the office setting (included in 63650)

MA criteria exceed NCD 160.7 (possible appeal basis under CMS-4201-F): MMP368.14 states a repeat trial after a failed trial is not appropriate unless extenuating circumstances led to the failure. Neither NCD 160.7 nor Palmetto LCD L37632 (v26) limits repeat trials. [uhc_ma_mmp368_14 vs NCD160.7, L37632]
Exceeds NCD 160.7 but matches Palmetto LCD L37632, so NOT an appeal basis in GA: trial must achieve ≥50% reduction of target pain or of analgesic medications.
Exceeds NCD 160.7 but matches L37632, so NOT an appeal basis in GA: trial must show some element of functional improvement.
Exceeds NCD 160.7 but matches L37632, so NOT an appeal basis in GA: chart documentation must support each trial-to-permanent-implant decision.
Same in NCD 160.7, L37632 and MMP368.14: multidisciplinary screening incl. psychological and physical evaluation; SCS as a late option after other modalities.
MMP368.14 applies its supplemental criteria only where no LCD/LCA exists. GA has Palmetto L37632 (+ billing article A56876), so L37632 is the controlling LCD for UHC MA in GA.
MMP368.14 and L37632 both say it is 'preferable' that the trialing physician implants the permanent device. Stated as a preference, not a coverage condition.

criteria.text: Moderate-to-severe low back pain primarily over the SIJ, between the upper iliac crests and the gluteal fold
Low back pain duration at least 3 months
Pain below L5 without radiculopathy

Clinical findings/imaging do not suggest another cause (central stenosis with claudication/myelopathy, foraminal stenosis or disc herniation with concordant radiculopathy, infection, tumor, fracture, pseudoarthrosis, hardware pain)
>=3 positive provocative maneuvers among FABER, Gaenslen, thigh thrust/posterior shear, SI compression, SI distraction, Yeoman
Pain persists despite at least 4 weeks of conservative therapy
Performed with conservative treatment; patient actively participating in rehab, home exercise, or functional restoration program
Coexisting psychological conditions/depression treated and stabilized before the procedure
CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (ultrasound only with documented contrast allergy or pregnancy)
Not performed with other lumbosacral musculoskeletal injections or other blocks in the same session or during the post-SIJI assessment period
Index pain measured pre-injection at start of session and post-injection at end of session, same scale
Diagnostic SIJI positive only if >=75% sustained relief of index pain for the duration of the anesthetic (and of the steroid), on the same scale, with dated measurements on the following days
No more than 2 diagnostic SIJI sessions (unilateral or bilateral); no subsequent diagnostic SIJI if the first gave <75% relief
Therapeutic SIJI only after a diagnostic SIJI with >=75% relief
Repeat therapeutic SIJI requires >=50% pain relief or >=50% ADL improvement for >=3 months from the prior SIJI vs baseline (same scale)
No more than 4 therapeutic SIJI sessions per rolling 12 months (each side on a separate day counts as a session)
SIJI beyond 12 months requires significant functional disability, >=50% sustained improvement for >=3 months, documented rationale, and PCP notification
Fluoroscopic images in >=2 views (pre/post contrast, AP and oblique) confirming intra-articular contrast retained
Relief documentation states specific dates, same scale, and whether duration is consistent with the agent used (a bare % is insufficient)
KX on diagnostic injections; physician bills 27096 (bilateral = modifier 50); hospital OPD/ASC facility bills G0260
